---
title: "Docker Compose"
---

The AI layer is composed of four profiles, to be started together with the rest of the stack (see [Docker Compose — Overview](../dev/docker-compose.qmd)):

| Profile | Service | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `neo4j-mcp` | `neo4j-mcp` | MCP toolbox exposing knowledge graph tools (port 5000, internal) |
| `crisalid-agents-owui` | `crisalid-agents-owui` | Graph agent served as OpenWebUI pipelines (port 9099, internal) |
| `crisalid-agents-chat-api` | `crisalid-agents-chat-api` | Graph agent served as a streaming chat API for SoVisuPlus (port 9100, internal) |
| `openwebui` | `openwebui` | User-facing chat UI |

Both agent services run the same CRISalid graph agent and require the `neo4j-mcp` profile (they wait for the toolbox to be healthy). Only start the wrapper(s) you actually use:

```bash
# OpenWebUI chat stack
docker compose \
  -f docker-compose.yaml \
  -f docker-compose.dev.yaml \
  --profile neo4j-mcp \
  --profile crisalid-agents-owui \
  --profile openwebui \
  up -d

# SoVisuPlus chat API
docker compose \
  -f docker-compose.yaml \
  -f docker-compose.dev.yaml \
  --profile neo4j-mcp \
  --profile crisalid-agents-chat-api \
  up -d
```

Configuration:

- Agent LLM and toolbox settings: `docker/crisalid-agents/.env` (shared by both agent services).
- Chat API key: the shared `SOVISUPLUS_CHAT_API_KEY` in `docker/.env`, injected into both the chat API and SoVisuPlus. See [Security](security.qmd).
- Assistant content (welcome message, prompt suggestions, agent system prompt): the `docker/sovisuplus/config/chat.json` file, see [below](#sovisuplus-assistant-content).
- OpenWebUI → pipelines connection: configured by hand in the admin panel, see [Configuring OpenWebUI](configuring-openwebui.qmd).

## SoVisuPlus assistant content {#sovisuplus-assistant-content}

The chat widget's **welcome message**, **prompt suggestions** and the agent's **system prompt** are not hardcoded in SoVisuPlus. They come from a JSON config file that SoVisuPlus reads server-side, so the same image can be deployed at any institution without a rebuild. The image carries a generic version of that file as a fallback; this section is about replacing it with your own.

::: {.callout-note}
## The widget only appears when the chat API is configured
SoVisuPlus renders the assistant only if `CRISALID_AGENTS_API_URL` is set (it defaults to `http://crisalid-agents-chat-api:9100` in `sovisuplus.yaml`) **and** a config file resolves. In Docker the second condition is normally met — the image ships a generic `chat.sample.json` as a last-resort fallback — but a config file that fails to parse counts as no config at all (see below). A `chat.json` on its own will not make the widget appear: the `crisalid-agents-chat-api` profile must be running too.
:::

### Where the file is read from

The file lives at `docker/sovisuplus/config/chat.json`, exactly like `rbac.roles.yaml` beside it: `docker/sovisuplus/config` is bind-mounted read-only at `/config`, and `sovisuplus.yaml` pins `CHAT_CONFIG_FILE=/config/chat.json` the same way it pins `RBAC_ROLES_FILE=/config/rbac.roles.yaml`. There is no environment variable for you to set.

SoVisuPlus checks each candidate for existence and takes the first that is there, so a missing file is not an error:

| # | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `/config/chat.json` | The mount, named by `CHAT_CONFIG_FILE`. **This is the one to edit.** |
| 2 | `/app/chat.json` | The app's own working-directory config. Unreachable through the `/config` mount, so unused in this deployment. |
| 3 | `/app/chat.sample.json` | Generic fallback baked into the image. |

Because `docker/sovisuplus/config` is already mounted, customising the assistant is a one-file change — no compose edit and no extra volume:

```bash
cp docker/sovisuplus/config/chat.sample.json docker/sovisuplus/config/chat.json
$EDITOR docker/sovisuplus/config/chat.json
```

The file is read **once per process and cached**, so a restart is required to pick up edits:

```bash
docker compose \
  -f docker-compose.yaml \
  -f docker-compose.dev.yaml \
  --profile sovisuplus \
  up -d sovisuplus
```

To roll back, delete `config/chat.json` and restart: resolution falls through to the baked `/app/chat.sample.json` and the widget keeps working.

### Schema

```json
{
  "systemPrompt": "Instructions that shape the agent's behaviour, for {{institutionName}}.",
  "variables": { "supportEmail": "svp-support@example.edu" },
  "locales": {
    "en": {
      "welcome": { "title": "Welcome", "message": "Hi! I'm your SoVisu+ assistant…" },
      "suggestions": [{ "label": "Open access rate", "value": "How many publications in my organization are open access?" }]
    },
    "fr": {
      "welcome": { "title": "Bienvenue", "message": "Bonjour ! Je suis votre assistant SoVisu+…" },
      "suggestions": [{ "label": "Taux de science ouverte", "value": "Combien de publications sont en science ouverte dans mon organisation ?" }]
    }
  }
}
```

| Field | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `systemPrompt` | Sent to the agent as a `role:"system"` message by the `/api/chat` proxy. **Layered after** the agent's own built-in prompt — it augments the agent, it does not replace it. Omit it or leave it empty to rely on the agent's default. |
| `variables` | Optional map of custom `{{key}}` values for `systemPrompt`, so the prompt can be parametrised by editing this file alone. Merged over the app-provided defaults, and able to override them. |
| `locales.<lang>.welcome` | Seeds the first assistant message when the widget opens; `title` names the conversation. |
| `locales.<lang>.suggestions` | Starter chips. `value` is the text submitted, `label` is what the user sees (`label` falls back to `value` when omitted). |

Locales are keyed by the language segment of the URL (`en`, `fr`, …). An unknown locale falls back to `en`, and then to empty values.

Every field is optional, so a config containing only the pieces you care about is valid.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Invalid JSON hides the assistant
A file that is unreadable or does not parse is logged as `[ChatConfigService] Could not load …` and treated as *no config at all* — the widget stops being rendered, rather than falling through to the baked fallback. Validate before restarting:

```bash
python3 -m json.tool docker/sovisuplus/config/chat.json > /dev/null && echo OK
```
:::

::: {.callout-important}
## The system prompt is server-only, the rest is public
`systemPrompt` is read in the Next.js server process and injected into the upstream request. It is **never** sent to the browser, so it is a reasonable place for instructions you would not want users to read or tamper with — but it is not a security boundary: it shapes agent behaviour and nothing more. Access control lives in [Security](security.qmd), and the `welcome`/`suggestions` strings *are* shipped to the browser.

Note that the proxy also injects the signed-in user's identity as a second system message, from the trusted session, so the agent can resolve "me"/"my" and scope graph queries to that person. That happens regardless of `chat.json`.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## The institution name fills itself in
`systemPrompt` supports `{{variable}}` placeholders, resolved server-side before the prompt is sent. The sample uses `{{institutionName}}`, which SoVisuPlus fills from `INSTITUTION_NAME` in `docker/.env` (passed through as `NEXT_PUBLIC_INSTITUTION_NAME` in `sovisuplus.yaml`) — so there is nothing to keep in sync by hand.

Any other key you need goes in the file's `variables` map. A placeholder that matches neither an app-provided default nor a `variables` entry resolves to an empty string, so a typo silently drops the text rather than leaking `{{...}}` to the agent.
:::
